answer: A slow-release staking vault makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock real funds for a long epoch before it can earn, so a Sybil farm pays the same bond per clone while an honest agent pays once. At the glacier pace of unlocks, an attacker spinning up thousands of clones faces a long capital freeze, and at the nadir of the market the locked stake still cannot be withdrawn to fund the next wave. The cost scales with each identity, so faking thousands costs thousands of bonds.
